migration.step: if (from < 13) { await m.createTable(tasksTable); } if (from < 14) { await m.createTable(recoveryProfilesTable); await m.createTable(avoidedHabitsTable); await m.createTable(urgeLogsTable); await m.createTable(dailyRitualsTable); await m.createTable(ritualLogsTable); await m.createTable(procrastinationLogsTable); } if (from < 15) { await m.addColumn(tasksTable, tasksTable.clientId); await m.addColumn(tasksTable, tasksTable.remoteId); }

_comment_tr_keys: Design strip section 47 (47a-47d, 47h, 47i): the compose lane's 'From template' row and its six chips, plus the one line frame 47d's gate says under them while the plant is not yet described. The composer injects these into base_sdk's TrKeys, so the installed tasks page reads them as TrKeys.<name>; this SDK's own lib never references them (its tests run on a bare checkout). Checked against base_sdk's hand-written keys and every other SDK manifest in the fleet: no collision. The step names and instructions inside the templates are DATA on the task map (paas_pos's own strings, verbatim), not copy, and carry no key.
_comment_routes_vision: Design strip section 41 (the M2 vision cluster, approved 2026-08-30): /vision hosts the plan on a page (41a) with the objective drill in its last plane (41b) and the stacked phone fold (41d); /vision/mastery hosts personal mastery (41c). Both are pushed pages from the productivity gate (approved 7e) and draw the corner back pill themselves. View-first: they read the productivity module's six get_* methods through the platform gateway and write nothing - the legacy add/edit dialogs are write endpoints to add at build time. Other SDKs open them by route path and never import productivity_sdk (ADR-005).
_comment_routes: Design strip section 46: /tasks/run?task=<id> hosts a task's guided run as a page of its own. On a wide window /tasks hosts the same TaskRunView in its detail plane (frame 46a, no new push); at one plane the workspace pushes this route (46f). Other SDKs open a run by route path and never import productivity_sdk (ADR-005). It pops true when the user marks the task done from the finished card.
_comment_integrations_vision: Design strip section 41: the two vision pages ride the same launcher glance entry as /tasks (two more GlanceCardItems, same route-path navigation, same missing-marker skip). The hub-side door - rows under the productivity group of the manager hub (approved 7e) - is the COMMERCE side of the section, like the tasks-row markers below, and is not in this release.
_comment_integrations: When the host also composes launch_sdk (its installed home page ships the '// @launcher-glance' marker at lib/presentation/pages/launch/home.dart), inject a permanent glance entry that opens this SDK's /tasks page - otherwise the launcher home has no visible way to reach tasks. The placeholder is the marker line INCLUDING its 12-space indent: update_layout_integrations() does a plain substring replace, and the bare marker text is also a prefix of the separate '// @launcher-glance-imports' marker at column 0, which must not match. GlanceCard/GlanceCardItem (base_sdk), RemixIcons and context.router are already imported by the launch home template, so no import injection is needed; navigation is by route path so this SDK still never imports launch_sdk (ADR-005). In hosts without launch_sdk the target file does not exist and the integration is skipped.
_comment_integrations_tasks_row: Design strip frame 46i (approved 2026-08-30; 47j folded into it 2026-08-31): the paused run announces itself on the door it lives behind - ONE LINE on the hub's existing Tasks row, not a new row and not a new group, gone when no run is paused. When the host composes merchants_sdk (its installed manager hub ships the '// @productivity-tasks-row' marker under the Tasks row of lib/presentation/pages/manager/restaurant/restaurant_page.dart, plus '// @productivity-tasks-row-imports' at column 0 among its imports), inject PausedRunLine there. Two entries because the line is this SDK's widget and the hub does not import productivity_sdk on its own: the imports marker takes the import, the row marker takes the widget. Same substring-replace rules as the launcher glance: the row placeholder carries its 8-space indent so it cannot match the column-0 imports marker, of which the bare marker text is a prefix. The line opens the run by ROUTE PATH ('/tasks/run?task=<id>', this SDK's own route) through context.router, which the hub already imports, so the hub never imports a page (ADR-005). Both markers are the COMMERCE side of the frame and land in the merchants repo; until they do, the composer reports the marker missing and skips the wiring, exactly as it does for a host without launch_sdk.
